description: Malay Basin Palynological Zonation — PR1 to PR15. Based on Yakzan et al. integrated biostratigraphic framework. Palynology is the backbone of Malay Basin biostratigraphy because much of the basin fill is non-marine to marginal marine. Pollen, spores, dinoflagellates, freshwater algae, and mangrove indicators provide age AND environment constraint.
source: Yakzan et al. — Integrated biostratigraphic zonation for the Malay Basin
basin_context: Oligocene to Pleistocene pull-apart / rift-sag basin. Non-marine to marginal marine with periodic marine incursions from the South China Sea. Up to 12 km of sediment.
confidence_caveat: PR zone ages are calibrated to seismic groups and regional unconformities, not to global chronostratigraphy alone. Age brackets are basin-specific and may not transfer to Sabah or Sarawak without recalibration.

seismic_groups.description: Malay Basin seismic groups A through M provide the structural-stratigraphic container. PR zones are tied to these groups.

upper_miocene_unconformity.description: Major basin-wide unconformity. Separates Groups D/E from C. Erosion or non-deposition.
upper_miocene_unconformity.biozone_signature: PR10/PR11 below, PR12/PR13 above — PR11 or PR12 may be missing

middle_miocene_unconformity.description: Separates upper Group C from Group B. Widespread erosion.
middle_miocene_unconformity.biozone_signature: May truncate PR13 or remove part of PR14

PR1.paleoenvironment: Fluvial to lacustrine, minor brackish influence
PR1.ecological_signal: Continental interior — freshwater algae (Pediastrum, Botryococcus) indicate lacustrine conditions
PR1.confusion_risk: May resemble younger lacustrine phases if marine markers are absent

PR2.ecological_signal: First marine incursion indicators — coastline approaching basin
PR2.confusion_risk: Marine signal may be subtle and diachronous

PR3.paleoenvironment: Marginal marine with periodic marine incursions
PR3.ecological_signal: Coastal/marginal marine established. Dinoflagellate cysts mark marine water entry.

PR4.paleoenvironment: Coastal to shallow marine, increasing marine influence
PR4.ecological_signal: Sustained marine connection. Marine flooding surfaces become reliable correlation markers.

PR5.ecological_signal: Fully marine shelf conditions established. Mangrove pollen from coastal belt.

PR6.ecological_signal: Open marine conditions. Maximum marine influence in basin center.

PR7.paleoenvironment: Open marine shelf to upper slope
PR7.ecological_signal: Deepening trend. May indicate early progradation setup.

key_markers: marine palynomorphs with terrestrial input increase
PR8.ecological_signal: Shelf/slope progradation begins. Terrestrial pollen input increases — sediment supply rising.

PR9.ecological_signal: Active progradation. Terrestrial signal dominant in proximal, marine in distal.

PR10.ecological_signal: High sediment supply. Pollen assemblages track vegetation belts and climate.

PR11.ecological_signal: Shallowing trend. May be truncated by Upper Miocene Unconformity in some areas.

PR12.ecological_signal: New depositional cycle above 10-10.5 Ma unconformity. Progradation resumes.

PR13.ecological_signal: Major progradational pulse. Coastal plain pollen assemblages. May be truncated by 7.8 Ma unconformity.

PR14.paleoenvironment: Upper progradational clastics, coastal to shallow marine
PR14.ecological_signal: Late-stage basin fill. High sedimentation rate. Climate cycling visible in pollen.

PR15.paleoenvironment: Youngest clastic wedge, coastal to marine
PR15.ecological_signal: Glacial/interglacial cycling visible. Sea-level fluctuations drive facies changes.

mangrove_pollen_increase.interpretation: Coastline proximity — mangroves indicate marginal marine/coastal setting
mangrove_pollen_increase.duration: May be diachronous as coastline migrates

marine_palynomorph_appearance.interpretation: Marine water entry into basin — flooding surface or transgression
marine_palynomorph_appearance.caution: May be older toward basin center, younger toward margin (diachronous)

peat_swamp_pollen_assemblage.interpretation: Coastal plain peat swamp — humid tropical climate, low-energy
peat_swamp_pollen_assemblage.not: Time marker — climate and sea-level controlled

pollen_climate_shift.interpretation: Climate-driven vegetation change — may not indicate age change
pollen_climate_shift.caution: Climate shifts can produce pollen changes that mimic biozone boundaries

cross_discipline_integration.with_nannofossils: PR4-PR5 corresponds to first consistent nannofossil occurrence. PR6-PR11 tied to NN5-NN11 equivalents. PR12-PR15 tied to NN12-NN21.
cross_discipline_integration.with_foraminifera: Planktonic forams appear with marine incursions from PR3 onward. Benthic forams track water depth through PR4-PR11.
cross_discipline_integration.with_seismic: PR zones are defined within seismic groups A-I. Major unconformities at ~10-10.5 Ma and ~7.8 Ma separate groups.
cross_discipline_integration.with_lithostratigraphy: PR1-PR2 = syn-rift to early post-rift clastics. PR3-PR7 = marine-influenced. PR8-PR15 = progradational clastic wedge.

constitutional_alignment.B7_Regional_Diachroneity: PR zone boundaries are tied to local Malay Basin calibration. Do not copy into Sabah or Sarawak without independent calibration.
constitutional_alignment.B6_MultiDiscipline_Convergence: PR zones must be cross-checked with nannofossils, forams, seismic groups, and lithostratigraphy. No PR zone alone certifies an age.
constitutional_alignment.F7_HUMILITY: Age brackets are approximate — calibrated to basin-scale unconformities and seismic groups, not global chronostratigraphy.
